## Celestial Return

_aka, "Syzygy"_

This is my second-largest mural to date, with "[Heart of the Rose](heart-of-the-rose)" still holding the heavyweight crown. It's an absolute beast of a piece -- packing in a combined total of 17 different fractals. It was so massive I actually had to call in backup from fellow fractalist Will Scates ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/willscates/)) just to help render the damn thing.

While it was originally created for the Desert Hearts festival in May of 2016, it's since become a part of the Mystic Flyer Experience ([Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/MysticFlyerExperience)) at Burning Man each year.

The centerpiece is easily the crowd favorite. I took "The Little Astronaut" and integrated it with "[A Ship for All Destinations](destination-everywhere)", finally adding "[The Lighthouse at the End of the Universe](other-fractalscapes)". And trust me, the planetary alignment and the cultural glyphs woven into it? None of that was chosen haphazardly. Every single line has intention.

The right panel is explicit -- highly luminescent and glowing with ever-present celestial light. The left side plays it smoother. It seamlessly blends subtle differences that actually make it the most mysterious piece of the triptych. We're talking feathers texturing the stars themselves, gravity wells circling outward in spirals down the arms, and nested circles diving infinitely deeper into their own cores.

It's a planetary alignment mapped out in sacred geometry... a syzygy of fractal stars caught in a celestial return to form the Eye of the Infinite itself. Inside one planet, a lighthouse shines out to cast its beam across the rest. In another, a massive steampunk vessel violently bursts through time and space. And in the final one? A tiny astronaut sits out in an open field, just staring up in absolute wonder at the stars above.

_Let no one ever steal your wonder._

Note: While the central alignment with the fractal planets is easily the crowd favorite and top-seller at the Redbubble link above, I did in fact get a special request a few years ago for the left panel, the "wormhole" portion of the three. Because of that, you can still find prints and other productst with it [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/46217803). The right panel isn't available anywhere for purchase, but it's based on my award-winning "Oz the Great & Powerful" design that you'll find [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23964488) (and also loosely related to the lesser known "Capax Infinitum, Carpe Noctum").

content.text:
## Mystic Flyer: Prehistory

To even get to the place of telling the modern story, there's a LOT of history that has to be covered. Camp Mystic founders Captain Niceguy and Cyberius Rex (not sure if Cosmic Cowboy was there) were at Island Fest where a dream was born. One of the busses at the festival was up for sale and needed some work. It didn't take much convincing to lock in that sell and hand over the license for the bus to Camp Mystic. After the festival, Cyberius drove it down to The Otto Ranch near Lander, Wyoming (where I first met her). They'd painted "Festibus" over the top of the front visor. With some fixes by Joel Otto, Tea Master got it down to Reno for us.

That brings us to my brother Skybreak and my sister Gaea pulling into Reno for crew on Camp Mystic in 2008. Skybreak and I cleaned the HELL outta the inside. _Nasty biz!_ Then Skybreak drove her into our camp's storage unit, where Gaea met up with us to pile the bus as high as we could. No, seriously, like up past the highest windows. Our lil game of Tetris had her weighed down but still kicking.

With a night of rest, fun, and respite... we began the trek out to Black Rock City the next day. Skybreak drove the beast, and lemme tell ya, "beast" is an understatement. That steering wheel borders on useless. Then we got stopped at the gate coming in. She was too packed for them to clear us. "If you can't open the back," the gate guard said, "we just can't let you in." They had to check inside her.

This became the now-legendary climb that Skybreak made over everything we'd packed in, himself jam-packed between the "stuff" and the roof, to make it all the way to the back of the bus and reach the latch. When that door fucking opened... when the guards could see inside.. . the roar of clapping and shouting that broke out to celebrate the amazing feat is a moment to be remembered for all time.

They didn't just clear us for passage into paradise, but in fact whooped and shouted us onward as we made our way onto the playa towards camp.

The Basura Sagrada -- the holiest site in time and space -- awaited us on the other side.

content.caption: Festibus loaded to the very top and ready to roll!

content.text:
## Mystic Flyer: Desert Hearts

As you've already seen my mural that spans the entire back of the "experience" at Desert Hearts, I wanted to show you one of the two different "All Seeing Eyes" made by Muséus ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/museusdance/)). By day, it provided shade and shelter to the community. It become something entirely different at night. It wouldn't be until later in 2016 that it would finally be joined with Festibus to create the second, and most long-lasting mutant vehicle for Camp Mystic. But we're getting ahead of ourselves.

## Mystic Flyer: The LED Panels

The famed LED panels for The Mystic Flyer made their debut with the "experience" at Desert Hearts. Cyberius Rex is the insane brain behind the electrical work... with the psytrance-scene legend Android Jones himself ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/android_jones/)) alongside him for the designs to move across each panel. At Desert Hears, the panels rotated inward, and outward, so that those within the walls would be bathed in their shifting patterns... taking them to space and beyond!

## Mystic Flyer: Mutant Vehicle Mode Engaged

The days of Festibus living only to haul camp equipment were numbered. With the success of the murals and overall experience at Desert Hearts, the two were on a collision course towards Black Rock City, Nevada for Burning Man. Cyberius Rex (+ an entire crew) got to welding while still in Reno, with a few other on-playa fixes before the big event. Android Jones returned, not only for the face-piece of the art car, but in fact added an incredibly detailed underpainting for the LED boards so give the bus a "day" and a "night" side. By day, it was a desert skiff hovering over the dust with crowds on two levels. By night it was a glowing, pulsing dance party on wheels.

She now sails yearly with Camp Mystic on the playa at Burning Man.
